digest.lead: Anthropic faces a trust crisis as reports emerge of unauthorized access to their Mythos model, with security concerns mounting around the Claude Desktop app's undisclosed browser integration.
digest.summary: Meanwhile, Claude Code received useful persistence updates for developer workflows, and Mozilla showcased Mythos' debugging capabilities by finding 271 Firefox bugs.

stories.headline: Security Concerns Mount Over Claude Desktop's Undisclosed Browser Integration
stories.summary: Claude Desktop app has been installing an undisclosed native messaging bridge that enables browser communication without explicit user consent [1]. The discovery has raised privacy and security questions about the app's permissions and data access capabilities.
key_points: Native messaging bridge installed without clear disclosure to users
Enables browser communication capabilities that weren't explicitly announced
stories.impact: Desktop users and security-conscious organizations may need to reassess Claude Desktop deployments and review browser integration permissions.

sources.title: Anthropic's Claude Desktop App Installs Undisclosed Native Messaging Bridge

stories.headline: Trust Crisis Emerges as Mythos Model Faces Unauthorized Access Reports
stories.summary: Multiple reports indicate Anthropic's Mythos model is being accessed by unauthorized users [1], leading to growing verification and trust concerns [2]. The incidents have sparked broader questions about Anthropic's security practices and model access controls.
key_points: Unauthorized access to Mythos model confirmed by multiple sources
Trust and verification issues affecting Anthropic's reputation
stories.impact: Enterprise customers evaluating Claude models may delay deployments pending security clarifications, while existing users reassess access controls.

sources.title: Anthropic's Mythos Model Is Being Accessed by Unauthorized Users
A Boy That Cried Mythos: Verification Is Collapsing Trust in Anthropic

stories.headline: Mozilla Demonstrates Mythos' Debugging Capabilities with 271 Firefox Bug Discoveries
stories.summary: Mozilla successfully used Anthropic's Mythos model to identify and fix 271 bugs in Firefox [1]. The collaboration showcases the model's potential for large-scale code analysis and quality assurance in major software projects.
stories.impact: Development teams at major software companies may accelerate Mythos adoption for automated bug detection and code quality initiatives.

sources.title: Mozilla Used Anthropic's Mythos to Find and Fix 271 Bugs in Firefox

stories.headline: Claude Code v2.1.119 Adds Persistent Settings and Enhanced PR Integration
stories.summary: The latest Claude Code release introduces persistent configuration storage in `~/.claude/settings.json` with project-level override support [1]. The update also expands pull request integration beyond GitHub to include GitLab merge requests and Bitbucket PRs, plus adds customizable PR review URL templates.
key_points: Settings now persist across sessions with hierarchical override support
Expanded PR integration for GitLab, Bitbucket, and GitHub Enterprise
Added environment variable to hide working directory in startup display
stories.impact: Daily Claude Code users will benefit from streamlined configuration management and broader git platform support, reducing setup friction in diverse development environments.

stories.headline: Configure persistent Claude Code settings using ~/.claude/settings.json
stories.summary: Claude Code now saves your /config preferences (theme, editor mode, verbose output) to a persistent file instead of resetting each session. This eliminates the need to reconfigure your preferences every time you start Claude Code.
actionable_steps: Run Claude Code and use /config to set your preferred theme, editor mode, and other settings
Verify settings are saved to ~/.claude/settings.json file
Test persistence by restarting Claude Code and confirming settings remain

stories.headline: Enable forked subagents in external Claude Code builds
stories.summary: Forked subagents allow Claude Code to spawn separate agent processes for parallel task execution. This can improve performance for complex workflows that benefit from concurrent processing.
actionable_steps: Restart Claude Code to apply the setting
Verify subagents are working by checking for multiple agent processes during complex tasks

stories.headline: Use visual mode in Claude Code for text selection and editing
stories.summary: Claude Code now supports vim-style visual mode (v) and visual-line mode (V) for selecting and manipulating text. This enables more efficient text editing workflows similar to vim editors.
actionable_steps: Press 'v' to enter visual mode for character-by-character selection
Press 'V' to enter visual-line mode for line-by-line selection
Use standard vim operators on your selected text

stories.headline: Use defer permission in PreToolUse hooks to pause headless sessions
stories.summary: You can now pause headless Claude Code sessions at tool calls and resume them later with permission evaluation. This allows for better control over automated workflows that need human approval.
actionable_steps: Set up a PreToolUse hook in your Claude Code configuration
Return 'defer' as the permission decision in the hook
The hook will re-evaluate the tool call upon resumption

stories.headline: Use environment variables to configure MCP server settings in Claude Code
stories.summary: Claude Code v2.1.85 introduced CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_SERVER_NAME and CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_SERVER_URL environment variables for MCP headersHelper scripts. This allows a single helper script to serve multiple MCP servers, simplifying configuration management.
actionable_steps: Set the CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_SERVER_NAME environment variable to your desired server name
Set the CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_SERVER_URL environment variable to your MCP server URL
Update your MCP headersHelper scripts to use these variables instead of hardcoded values
